desc: The only independent federal audit of the records surrounding the founding event of this entire subject, produced by GAO at the direction of Representative Steven H. Schiff of New Mexico and issued on 28 July 1995. GAO did not investigate what crashed; it investigated what paper survived. Its findings are stark and have never been rebutted. Roswell Army Air Field administrative records covering March 1945 to December 1949, and RAAF outgoing messages covering October 1946 to December 1949, had been destroyed - and 'the document disposition form does not indicate what organization or person destroyed the records and when or under what authority the records were destroyed.' The entire government-wide search yielded two records originating in 1947. GAO's list of the record sets it searched includes the Air Force Safety Agency at Kirtland, the Air Force History Support Office at Bolling, Army Counterintelligence Corps holdings at Carlisle and Fort Meade, CIA at Langley, and - notably - NSA at Fort Meade under the heading 'FOIA records, Citizens Against UFO Secrecy.' A destruction of four years of one installation's outgoing traffic with no recorded authority is, in federal records terms, an unexplained event. GAO said so in 1995 and no one has explained it since.

entityInfo.desc: GAO's report is the closest thing to a neutral federal referee this subject has ever had, and its findings are narrow, verifiable and damning. It was requested by Rep. Steven Schiff and issued 28 July 1995. GAO searched Air Force, Army, Navy, FBI, CIA, NSA, National Archives and presidential library holdings. It reported: that in 1947 Army regulations required air accident reports to be maintained permanently but that no military service filed a report on the Roswell incident and there was no requirement to report a weather balloon crash; that 'although some of the records concerning Roswell activities had been destroyed, there was no information available regarding when or under what authority the records were destroyed'; that only two government records originating in 1947 were recovered; and, specifically, that 'RAAF administrative records (from Mar. 1945 through Dec. 1949) and RAAF outgoing messages (from Oct. 1946 through Dec. 1949) were destroyed.' The disposition form for that destruction records neither the organisation nor the person responsible, nor the date, nor the authority. In federal records terms that is not an anomaly; it is a defect. Four years and three months of one installation's outgoing message traffic, spanning the exact window in question, eliminated with no accountable authority. GAO also documented that a July 1947 FBI record showed the military had reported an object 'resembling a high-altitude weather balloon' - and that this was one of only two 1947-origin records the entire government could produce.
